standard_prerequisites.name: Initial sequents
standard_prerequisites.statement: The sequent !A sequent !A is an initial sequent and hence derivable in the sequent calculus.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the derivation used in the proof (712-713).

standard_prerequisites.name: Derivability from a set of sentences
standard_prerequisites.statement: Gamma proves !A when some finite Gamma_0 subset of Gamma has the sequent Gamma_0 sequent !A derivable.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof closes the gap between the initial sequent and derivability from the arbitrary set Gamma (712-714).

core_obligations: The initial sequent !A sequent !A is derivable (712-713).
Since {!A} is a finite subset of Gamma, the definition of derivability from a set yields Gamma proves !A (713-714).

proof_roadmap.step: Derive the singleton initial sequent and apply the definition.

difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 706-709: if !A is in Gamma then Gamma proves !A. The author proof (711-714) is complete in one step: the initial sequent !A sequent !A is derivable by the identity axiom, and the singleton {!A} is a finite subset of Gamma. Nothing is omitted.
